name: Supercomputer: Exascale FLOPS Desk — Simple
title: Supercomputer: Exascale FLOPS Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] FLOPS are cores × clock × FLOPs/cycle: the desk computes the peak and the sustained (HPL) for any system. A million cores at 2 GHz doing 16 FLOP/cycle is 32 exaflops peak — the arithmetic of the Top500.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Peak: 1e6 cores x 2 GHz x 16 FLOP/cycle = 0.032 EFLOPS. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Supercomputer: Parallelization Failure vs. Fixed Core Allocation
real_world_basis: FLOPS budgeting is the real basis of supercomputer design.
signature_version: Signature version: the fixed-allocation FLOPS desk — the chapter's Fixed Core Allocation as the efficiency target, with the manifestation framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: the sustained number is the computer — peak is the brochure.
math_note: Peak: 1e6 cores x 2 GHz x 16 FLOP/cycle: 0.032 EFLOPS [verified]; Sustained at 65% efficiency: 20.8 EFLOPS [verified]

math_check.label: Peak: 1e6 cores x 2 GHz x 16 FLOP/cycle
math_check.note: corrected 2026-10-19: was '32 EFLOPS' — that is PFLOPS; 0.032 EFLOPS

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a procurement justified by peak.
how_it_works: Multiply cores, clock, and per-cycle FLOPs for the peak; apply the measured efficiency for the sustained. The demo budgets three systems.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
Every numerical claim recomputed at build time
